pr.title: List a page's sections and a nested project's neighbors in its sidebar
pr.head: b676859f835f676e451dd76383ee057bff555121

summary: A project page on the Projector site shows a plan beside a sidebar, drawn the way a pull request summary's sidebar is: the project's stacks of pull requests, then the project's other pages. Unlike a summary's sidebar, it has no list of the page's sections, so on a plan of 500 to 800 lines you scroll to find a section. A nested project's sidebar also has no link to its parent or to its sibling projects, so you go through the breadcrumbs.

This pull request adds both. The sidebar lists the page's ## headings, read from the page after it renders, with the plan's own number in a column of its own. A nested project's sidebar ends with its parent project over the parent's other nested projects. One helper, watchSections, marks the section in view as you scroll, on project pages and on summary pages. At 980 pixels and narrower, the list starts folded behind a Sections toggle.
The build and site.json do not change: everything happens in the browser, in the TypeScript under site/src/ and its compiled copies under site/assets/.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Section: a top-level ## heading of a rendered page, or a group on a summary page.
  • Mark: aria-current="location" on the sidebar link to the section in view, drawn as a band with an accent bar.
  • The line: a horizontal line 30% of the way down the window. The marked section is the last one whose top has passed it.
  • Neighbors: a nested project's parent and the parent's other nested projects.

cards.title: Review status
cards.html: The Projector review of b676859 opened one P2 finding: a jump that carries a heading past the line in one frame, such as a link to a ### heading or the Home key, is never reported, so a plan's mark goes stale or missing. It is flagged under site/src/summary.ts. The validation gate passes, and the compiled scripts match the TypeScript.

groups.title: The shared section list and the watch
groups.kicker: Helpers that summary pages and project pages both use
intro: summary.ts holds helpers that every site page loads before site.js. This group adds two of them. sectionListHtml draws a list of sections, with the summary's reviewed dots or without them. watchSections marks the link to the section in view and keeps the mark current as the page scrolls.

The watch uses two IntersectionObservers and no scroll listener. The first watches each section's target against the top 30% of the window, and the second watches a zero-height marker placed after the sections, so that a short last section can still be marked at the end of the page. Each report reads every target's position again and moves the mark.

files.note: Adds PageSection: a section's id, its number or an empty string, and its title as markup.
Adds sectionListHtml and watchSections, and the summary page draws and watches its list with them.

checks.text: Open P2 finding: passing reports a heading only when it enters or leaves the top 30% band, so a jump that carries a heading from below the line to above the window in one frame is never reported. In headless Chrome 151, a jump into the middle of a long section left no row marked, and a jump back to the top left the old mark in place. The suggested fix extends the band above the page with rootMargin: '100000px 0px -70% 0px', which fixed both jumps in the same test.
At the end of a scrolled page, the line drops to the window's bottom, because a short last section never reaches the 30% line before the page stops scrolling.
The summary's list is the markup it drew before, plus class="sections" on the <ol>; SectionWatchTests asserts the exact markup, and the suite passes at this head.

files.note: Draws the mark: the row's hover band with an accent bar at its start.

groups.title: The project page sidebar
groups.kicker: Sections, a nested project's neighbors, and the narrow-screen toggle
intro: A project page draws its sidebar twice: once while the Markdown loads, and again once it renders. showDocument now passes the sidebar as a function of the page's sections, so the second drawing can list the headings the render produced, with the ids the render gave them. An HTML page lists no sections.

projectNav puts the readme's sections in their own block between the stacks and the pages. On a supplemental page, the sections open under that page's entry in the pages, through a new under argument to tree. A nested project's sidebar then ends with its neighbors, found by parentOf, the deepest project whose folder holds the nested project's folder.

checks.text: frame stops the watch before it draws any view, and showDocument starts it again after the render, so only one list is watched at a time.

files.note: Reads the rendered sections, draws the new sidebar blocks, and flips the Sections toggle.

checks.text: sectionsOf takes only top-level <h2> elements, so a heading inside a quote is not listed. A leading number such as 2. or 2.1 moves to the number column, and a year such as 2026 roadmap stays in the title.

Links are stripped with a regular expression over the heading's markup. Current Chrome escapes < inside attribute values, so the expression only meets real tags there. The review suggests unwrapping links in a cloned heading instead.

parentOf drops the folder's trailing slash before it calls ownerOf, so the project never finds itself. The nested-project tests in ProjectPageTests pass, including a grandchild that stays out of the neighbors.

files.note: Dividers for the new blocks, a two-column row for a plan's sections, and the toggle that folds them at 980 pixels and narrower.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Page, watch, and style tests under node
intro: The page tests run the compiled showProjectFile under node with a stub DOM. The watch tests run watchSections with a stub IntersectionObserver and call its callbacks directly, so they check the marking rule but not which scrolls the browser reports.

groups.title: The plan and the CLI docs
groups.kicker: The settled plan, marked completed, and the site description
intro: The plan project-page-sections records each question, its options, and the owner's decision, then the sidebar those decisions make. It ends completed, with an outcome section that lists the browser checks. docs/cli.md describes the new sidebar.

checks.text: § 2.10 says the observer reports each target that crosses the line or the window's top. A target that jumps across the band in one frame is not reported, which is the open finding.
